name: AI images
title: AI image prompt templates
seoTitle: AI Image Prompts: 6 Templates With Examples
description: Free AI image prompt templates for Midjourney, DALL·E, Gemini and other generators: product shots, portraits, consistent series and readable text in images.
intro: Strong image prompts name four things separately: subject, scene, style and framing. These templates keep those slots apart, so you can change one at a time and see exactly what it did.

templates.title: The four-slot base prompt
templates.useWhen: Any image — start here and change one slot at a time.
templates.prompt:
Subject: [WHO OR WHAT, with 2–3 concrete details]
Scene: [WHERE, time of day, weather or setting details]
Style: [PHOTO / ILLUSTRATION / 3D RENDER + one reference quality, e.g. “editorial magazine photo”]
Framing: [SHOT TYPE, e.g. close-up or wide], [CAMERA ANGLE], [ASPECT RATIO, e.g. 4:5]
Lighting: [e.g. soft window light from the left]
templates.why: Separate slots let you iterate one variable at a time. Vague prompts mix them, so you cannot tell which word changed the picture.

templates.title: Product photo on a clean background
templates.useWhen: Shop listings, landing pages and ads.
templates.prompt: Product photo of [PRODUCT, material, colour], centred, on a seamless [BACKGROUND COLOUR] background. Soft studio lighting from above with a gentle shadow under the product. Sharp focus on [KEY DETAIL, e.g. the label]. Straight-on angle at product height. Square 1:1. No text, no props, no extra objects.
templates.why: Product shots fail on clutter and invented text. The explicit “no text, no props” line is a negative constraint most generators respect.

templates.title: Natural portrait
templates.prompt: Portrait of [PERSON: age range, expression, clothing — never a real person's name], [SETTING]. Head-and-shoulders framing, eye level, 85mm lens look with a softly blurred background. [LIGHTING, e.g. warm late-afternoon light]. Natural skin texture, realistic proportions. Vertical 4:5.
templates.why: Lens and framing words are shorthand generators understand. Leaving out real names avoids likeness and policy problems.

templates.title: A consistent series of images
templates.useWhen: Several images must look like they belong together.
templates.prompt:
Create image [N] of a series. Keep IDENTICAL across the series: [CHARACTER OR PRODUCT DESCRIPTION], [COLOUR PALETTE], [STYLE], [LIGHTING].
Change only: [WHAT CHANGES IN THIS IMAGE, e.g. the pose or the location].
[If your tool supports it, attach the previous image as a reference.]
templates.why: Series drift happens when every prompt is rewritten. Copying the fixed block word for word and changing one line keeps the look stable.

templates.title: Poster or image with readable text
templates.useWhen: Posters, thumbnails and social graphics with a headline.
templates.prompt: Poster, [STYLE]. The only text is the headline “[EXACT TEXT, max 5 words]” in [FONT STYLE, e.g. bold sans-serif], [POSITION, e.g. top third], high contrast against the background. Background: [SCENE]. No other words, letters or logos anywhere.
templates.why: Generators misspell long text. Short exact wording in quotes, one position and “no other words” give the best odds — always proofread the result.

templates.title: Fix one thing in an image
templates.prompt:
Keep everything in this image the same except: [ONE CHANGE, e.g. make the sky overcast].
Do not change: [THE PARTS THAT MUST STAY — subject, composition, colours].
[Attach the image and use your tool's edit or inpaint mode if it has one.]
templates.why: Editing one variable at a time is the image version of iterating from the output. Listing what must stay stops the model re-rolling the whole picture.
